volume: Search volume: how many times a month the keyword is searched in the chosen country, averaged over the last 12 months.
kd: Keyword difficulty (0–100): how hard it is to reach the top 10, based on the link strength of the pages ranking there. Under 30 is easy, over 70 very hard.
cpc: Cost per click: what advertisers pay on average for one click on this keyword; a sign of its commercial value.
competition: Ad competition (0–1): how many advertisers bid on this keyword.
intent: Search intent: what the searcher wants. Informational (learn), navigational (find a site), commercial (compare) or transactional (buy).
traffic: Estimated organic traffic: monthly visits worked out from rankings, search volumes and the click rate of each position. For real visits see Search Console or GA4.
traffic_value: Traffic value: what this organic traffic would cost per month as ads (estimated clicks × CPC).
organic_keywords: Organic keywords: how many keywords the domain ranks for in Google's top 100.
position: Position: the place among organic results (ads and special boxes are not counted).
oa: OctopusOn Authority (OA, 0–100): the strength of a domain's or page's backlink profile. It is logarithmic: going from 60 to 70 is much harder than from 20 to 30.
backlinks: Backlinks: the total number of links from other sites to this site or page.
referring_domains: Referring domains: how many different domains link to this site at least once. It usually matters more for rankings than the total number of backlinks.
dofollow: Dofollow: links that pass strength to search engines (not marked nofollow, ugc or sponsored).
spam_score: Spam score (0–100): how likely a link or domain is artificial or low quality. Over 60 deserves a look.
anchor: Anchor: the clickable text of a link. A natural profile is mostly brand names and varied wording.
visibility: Visibility: the share of the clicks your tracked keywords could bring that you get, weighting each position by its click rate; 100% would mean first place everywhere.
average_position: Average position: the mean place of your tracked keywords that rank. Lower is better.
share_of_voice: Share of voice: your percentage of the visibility (or of the mentions in AI answers) shared by you and your competitors.
serp_features: SERP features: the special boxes on a result page: AI Overview, featured snippet, People also ask, local pack, images, videos…
ai_overview: AI Overview: the AI summary Google shows above the results. The sites it cites can get clicks from it.
mention_rate: Mention rate: the share of AI answers that name your brand.
citation_rate: Citation rate: the share of AI answers that link to your site as a source.
clicks: Clicks: real clicks from Google results to your site (Search Console).
impressions: Impressions: how many times your site appeared in Google results (Search Console).
ctr: CTR (click-through rate): clicks ÷ impressions. Below the usual rate for that position, the title and description can be improved.
health: Site health (0–100): a score of the errors and warnings on the crawled pages, weighted by priority.
geo_readiness: GEO readiness (0–100): how ready the site is to be read and cited by assistants such as ChatGPT and Gemini (AI crawler access, structured data, quotable content…).
top3_top10: Top 3 / top 10: how many keywords rank in these places. Most clicks go to the first three results.
paid_traffic: Paid traffic: the estimated monthly clicks the domain gets from Google Ads.
new_lost: New / lost: keywords that started ranking or dropped out since the last update (or links won and lost).
